title: Does the OmS layer pay for itself against plain OmO and bare opencode?
hypothesis: With the same task packs and the same Token Pass budget, opencode with the OmS layer (routing brain, ZDR rules, receipts) matches stock OmO on accepted rate and costs at least 30% less per accepted task, with zero ZDR violations, and both beat bare opencode on the agentic traps.
human_gate: Frank approves the spend (Token Pass cap) and any new install; arms run in the Railway container, not on the laptop.

runs_on.why: Same clean image for every arm, so differences come from the layer and not from the machine. Keeps load off the YELLOW-zone laptop.

arms.model: one fixed model chosen in EXP-001
routing brain chain per task class
arms.role: challenger: our layer, generated from routing.schema.json

suite: starlight-core-v0 + agentic-traps-v0 + web-v0 (structure, responsive and a11y tasks only)
success_rule: OmS is kept as a named layer only if accepted_rate is within 3 points of stock OmO, cost_per_accepted is at least 30% lower, zdr_violations is 0, receipt_completeness is 100%, and trap_pass_rate is not lower. If OmS only matches on cost, the value is governance and receipts, and that is stated as the result, not as a quality win.
kill: Stop at $4 of Token Pass or when two arms cannot run headless. Any arm with telemetry we cannot disable is dropped. With fewer than 10 runs per cell the report says directional and decides nothing.

next_gate.receipt: lab/results/EXP-008.md with the arm table, intervals and the pre-registration

decision_it_feeds: Whether OmS ships as a product layer, and what starlight-ai-harness (the public template) claims about itself.
preconditions: Pre-register the hypothesis, the prediction and the falsifier before the first run (SIS R5-DESIGN.md is the template).
Same tasks, same order, same wall-clock budget per task for every arm; paired comparison.
Regenerate the OmS config from the merged routing schema; do not run omo setup against a config holding live keys.

prior_evidence.claim: A single-sample probe found 3 of 4 rails passed 4 of 4 toy tasks and one free model returned an empty response on the puzzle.
prior_evidence.caveat: n=1 per cell, toy tasks, model rails not harness loops. It shows the battery works, not who is better.
